raw_case_text:
A 74-year old black male was referred to the Dr George Mukhari Hospital in Ga Rankuwa, Pretoria with midline facial destruction (Figure 1).
The patient stated that about a year before, a small growth had appeared on his nose, became ulcerated and then enlarged progressively. As the lesion enlarged, his nose became blocked with a discharge, he frequently had headaches, and the sight of his left eye deteriorated. However, owing to his destitute circumstances, it was about a year before he was brought to hospital. He does not smoke or drink alcohol, and had been in good health until the facial condition started.
On admission to hospital he had a fever, headache, conjunctivitis, swelling of the eyelids and of the lower part of the nose, and destruction of the entire midface with indurated swelling of the surrounding tissues (Figure 1). There were no intraoral or extra-facial cutaneous lesions, the regional lymph nodes were not enlarged, and clinically and radiologically the chest was normal.
Intravenous fluids and antibiotics were given and daily irrigation of the wound was started. The patient was not anaemic, was HIV-seronegative and did not have syphilis. There was leucocytosis but not lymphocytosis, and the erythrocyte sedimentation rate, C-reactive protein and lactate dehydrogenase were elevated. Serum IgG was present, but not IgM to EBV cuspid antigen.
Computed tomographic (CT) scans showed radiopacity of a degree consistent with a soft tissue encroachment in the nasal cavity, both maxillary sinuses, ethmoidal, frontal and sphenoidal sinuses, and the nasopharynx (Figures 2 and 3).
Biopsy of the tissue from the nasal mass showed a dense polymorphic cell infiltrate consisting of histiocytes, eosinophils and a great number of atypical lymphoid cells in an angiocentric distribution. The atypical lymphoid cells exhibited large nuclei, hyperchromatism, and some of them exhibited abnormal mitotic figures (Figure 4A). Areas of necrosis were evident.
Immunophenotypically, the tumour cells were positive for CD3 and CD56 (Figure 4B), but negative for CD20. Some of the large atypical lymphocytes were positive for CD30.
No facilities were available for in situ hybridization analysis which might have demonstrated whether the malignant cells harboured EBV small-encoded RNA.
As the clinical and histological features were consistent with a diagnosis of extranodal NK/T cell lymphoma, nasal type, the patient was referred to the oncology department for treatment, but he died soon after.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 74-year-old Black male presented with a 1-year history of a progressively enlarging, ulcerated nasal mass resulting in extensive midline facial destruction, nasal obstruction, purulent discharge, headaches, and left visual loss.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Approximately 1 year prior to admission, the patient noticed a small growth on his nose that ulcerated and progressively enlarged, causing nasal obstruction, nasal discharge, frequent headaches, and deteriorating vision in his left eye. Due to destitution, hospital presentation was delayed for 1 year.
subjective.past_medical_history: Previously healthy; non-smoker and non-drinker from a destitute socioeconomic background.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, headache, left visual deterioration, nasal blockage/discharge, eyelid swelling, and massive midfacial ulceration.

objective.physical_examination: The patient was febrile with conjunctivitis, bilateral eyelid and lower nasal edema, and extensive necrotic destruction of the entire midface with indurated surrounding soft-tissue swelling. No intraoral or extrafacial skin lesions or regional lymphadenopathy were present, and chest examination was normal.
objective.routine_investigations: Laboratory studies showed leukocytosis (without lymphocytosis), normal hemoglobin, elevated ESR, elevated CRP, and elevated LDH. HIV and syphilis serologies were negative, and serum EBV viral capsid antigen IgG was positive (IgM negative). Chest radiograph was normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Craniofacial CT demonstrated extensive soft-tissue opacification and destruction involving the nasal cavity, bilateral maxillary, ethmoidal, frontal, and sphenoidal sinuses, and the nasopharynx. Nasal mass biopsy histopathology and immunohistochemistry revealed a dense angiocentric polymorphic infiltrate with necrosis and large hyperchromatic atypical lymphoid cells with abnormal mitotic figures that stained positive for CD3, CD56, and focal CD30, and negative for CD20.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Confirmed nasal-type extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma (lethal midline granuloma; tertiary gummatous syphilis and HIV excluded via negative serologies and CD3+/CD56+ angiocentric lymphoma immunophenotyping). Managed initially with intravenous fluids, empiric antibiotics, and daily wound irrigation, and referred to oncology, but the patient died shortly thereafter.
